title: Greenfield Rust CLI tool: count lines, words, and chars in files (wc-lite)
description: Build a Rust CLI tool from scratch that counts lines, words, and characters in one or more files — similar to Unix wc.

task_spec.prompt:
Create a Rust CLI tool from scratch: Cargo.toml (name='wc-lite', edition=2021) and src/main.rs plus src/lib.rs.

Library (src/lib.rs): Define a struct Counts { lines: usize, words: usize, chars: usize } and a function count_file(path: &std::path::Path) -> std::io::Result<Counts> that reads the file and counts lines (newline-separated), whitespace-separated words, and total characters (Unicode scalar values).

Binary (src/main.rs): Accept one or more file paths as positional CLI arguments (use std::env::args). For each file, call count_file and print a line: '<lines> <words> <chars> <filename>'. If no files given, print usage to stderr and exit with code 1. If a file cannot be read, print an error to stderr and continue with remaining files.

Tests (in src/lib.rs #[cfg(test)]): Write at least three unit tests using a temporary string buffer (not real files — use std::io::Cursor and refactor count_file to accept impl Read if needed, or write a count_str(s: &str) -> Counts helper): test empty string, test single-line string, test multi-line string. cargo test must pass.
required_artifacts: src/lib.rs with Counts struct and count function
success_criteria: count_file correctly counts lines, words, and chars
CLI handles multiple files and missing-file errors gracefully
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
